newsitem.title: USA: Plane makes unscheduled landing after bomb threat.
newsitem.headline: Plane makes unscheduled landing after bomb threat.

text.p: An American Airlines plane with 69 people on board was forced to make an unscheduled landing Wednesday night because of a bomb threat, but a search found no evidence of any explosive, officials said Thursday.

American Flight 926, a Boeing 727 on its way to Detroit from Miami, landed at Jacksonville International Airport at about 9:00 p.m. EDT (0100 GMT Thursday), said Kathleen Bergen, a spokeswoman for the Federal Aviation Administration in Atlanta.
"The pilot reported a bomb threat," she said.
Bergen said she could give no more information about the threat. Police said no arrest was made. Comment from the airline was not immediately available.
The passengers left the plane, which was searched by airport police with dogs, said Robert Peek, a spokesman for the Jacksonville Port Authority.
"We had our airport police and our airport dogs go through the plane. They went through it thoroughly and did not find anything," he said.
He said another aircraft was brought in and the passengers left Jacksonville at about midnight EDT (0400 GMT). He said the original plane had also left the airport by Thursday afternoon.
American Airlines is a unit of AMR Corp.
